page: Amazon Web Services t4g.2xlarge is an ARM-based burstable general purpose instance powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 8 physical cores and 8 vCPUs utilizing the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture running at 2.5 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per core). As an arm64 system managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it includes dedicated L1d (64 KB), L2 (1.0 MB), and L3 (32 MB) caches, alongside hardware AES support. The instance lacks dedicated local storage and GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage and standard compute pathways with a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a distinction between multi-core efficiency and single-threaded performance. The instance demonstrates solid multi-core throughput, scoring 12133.02 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 5149.0 in multi-core Geekbench, supported by a 7972.0 Clang compilation score. Memory bandwidth reaches 114.09 GB/sec on large block reads and 53.44 GB/sec on writes. However, single-core processing is limited, reflected in an 877.0 Geekbench single-core score and low single-threaded compression benchmarks (7.11 GB/sec bzip3 decompression). Workloads demanding high vectorized throughput or intensive floating-point execution, such as LLM text generation, register in the lower tiers.

Cost efficiency is driven by the resource density of AWS Graviton silicon under a burstable allocation model. By leveraging a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio across 8 full physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, the t4g.2xlarge delivers affordable scaling for variable loads. It achieves 9.35 million Redis SET operations per second and 9.19 GB/sec in static web serving, making it well-suited for web servers, microservices, mid-tier caching layers, relational database replicas, and continuous integration runners that do not require sustained 100% CPU utilization.
description: Amazon Web Services t4g.2xlarge is an arm64 burstable general purpose instance powered by an 8-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz and 32.0 GB of memory. Operating under the AWS Nitro hypervisor, each vCPU maps directly to a physical core without multithreading. It includes no local storage and no GPUs, using a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate steady middle-tier multi-core and memory subsystem performance, reaching 12133.02 in stress-ng multi-core and 9.35 million Redis SET operations per second, though single-core and compression metrics fall into lower brackets. The t4g.2xlarge provides strong resource density and cost efficiency for burstable workloads, web serving, microservices, and development environments.
